image_description: A close-up view of a grey whale's tail flukes emerging from the ocean surface. The flukes are dark grey/black with a smooth texture, showing a central notch and broad span. Water is splashing vigorously around the base of the tail where it breaks the surface. The background consists of choppy, grey-blue sea water. No head, blowholes, or dorsal knuckles are visible in this specific crop.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The skin texture on the flukes is exceptionally smooth and uniform, lacking the subtle micro-texture, scars, or barnacle remnants often seen on real grey whales. It has a slight 'plastic' or airbrushed quality common in AI generations.

The water splash droplets on the left side appear somewhat frozen and lack coherent motion blur. Some droplets seem to float without clear trajectory or connection to the main splash mass, indicating minor physics simulation issues.
The background water texture is slightly repetitive and lacks deep perspective falloff, appearing as a flat pattern rather than a vast ocean surface.
